summary: Verified against primary PDFs (NTA JEE Main 2026 Information Bulletin, NTA NEET UG 2026 Information Bulletin, and the actual JEE Advanced 2026 Paper 1 & Paper 2 question papers from jeeadv.ac.in), not aggregator snippets. JEE Main 2026 Paper 1: 3 subjects x (Section A = 20 MCQ + Section B = 5 numerical), 75 questions, 300 marks, 180 min; Section B optional-choice is GONE (removed 2025) and Section B now carries -1 negative marking; NVQ answers must be "rounded off to the nearest integer". JEE Advanced 2026 (IIT Roorkee, 17 May 2026) is asymmetric: Paper 1 = 48 Q / 180 marks (per subject: 4 single-correct +3/0/-1; 4 multi-correct +4 with +3/+2/+1 partial and -1; 4 numerical to TWO decimals +4/0 with NO negative; 4 Matching List +4/0/-1), Paper 2 = 54 Q / 180 marks (4 single-correct; 5 multi-correct; 5 numerical; 2 question-stems x 2 numerical sub-questions at +2 each). Critically, the multi-correct penalty changed from -2 (2025 and earlier) to -1 in 2026, and Paper 1 dropped paragraph-type entirely — the pattern is genuinely not fixed year to year, so the marking rules MUST be data-driven per test, never hardcoded. NEET UG 2026 has no Section A/B at all: 180 compulsory questions, 720 marks, 180 minutes (14:00-17:00), +4/-1/0, pen-and-paper OMR, 13 languages; NEET 2026 was cancelled (3 May) and re-run on 21 June 2026, and NEET moves to CBT from 2027. Calculators are prohibited in JEE Main (NTA Public Notice 02 Nov 2025 called the Appendix-VIII on-screen-calculator line a typographic error) and in JEE Advanced — only an on-screen virtual numeric keypad exists. The NTA CBT console spec is fully documented in Appendix-VIII of the JEE Main bulletin: server-set countdown timer, 5-state question palette, Save & Next / Mark for Review & Next / Clear Response, palette-click navigation that does NOT save, free section switching, auto-advance on last question of a section, disabled physical keyboard, dark/light mode, font scaling and screen magnifier, and auto-submit at zero. Normalisation is percentile-per-shift on the TOTAL raw score to 7 decimal places (never an average of subject percentiles), with distinct tie-break chains for JEE Main (Maths→Phy→Chem→incorrect:correct ratios→same rank), JEE Advanced (positive marks→Maths→Physics→same rank) and NEET (Bio→Chem→Phy→incorrect:correct ratios→random by expert committee; age criterion abolished 2023).

findings.title: JEE Main 2026 Paper 1 structure is fixed at 75 Q / 300 marks with NO optional questions in Section B
findings.detail: Official Information Bulletin JEE (Main) 2026, section 2.4: per subject Section A = 20 MCQs, Section B = 05 numerical-value questions, 100 marks each for Mathematics, Physics, Chemistry. Total = 75 questions, 300 marks. Verbatim: 'There will be negative marking for incorrect answer in Section A and Section B. For each question in Section B, a candidate has to enter the correct integer value of the answer using the mouse and the on-screen virtual numeric keypad... For Section B, the answer should be rounded off to the nearest integer.' The COVID-era 10-questions-attempt-any-5 choice was scrapped from JEE Main 2025 and is absent in the 2026 bulletin. Marking: MCQ +4 / -1 / 0 (unanswered or Marked for Review without selecting an option); NVQ +4 / -1 / 0 (unanswered or Marked for Review without filling a numerical value). Duration 03 hours (180 min); 04 hours for PwD/PwBD eligible for a scribe. Shifts 09:00-12:00 and 15:00-18:00 IST. Paper 2A/2B = 210 min.
findings.implication: Our JEE Main blueprint generator must emit exactly 3 sections x (20 MCQ + 5 NVQ), all 25 compulsory, with per-question-type marking rows stored in DB (not constants). NVQ answer storage must be an INTEGER with an equality check after rounding-to-nearest-integer of the student's entry — do NOT allow decimals or tolerance ranges for JEE Main (unlike JEE Advanced).

findings.title: JEE Advanced 2026 Paper 1 exact section spec (parsed from the real paper, not a secondary summary)
findings.detail: jeeadv.ac.in/documents/p1_english.pdf, per subject (Mathematics, Physics, Chemistry — identical structure, 60 marks each, 180 total, 48 questions): SECTION 1 (Max 12): FOUR questions, four options, ONLY ONE correct. Full +3 / Zero 0 if unanswered / Negative -1 in all other cases. SECTION 2 (Max 16): FOUR questions, ONE OR MORE THAN ONE correct. Full +4 only if all correct chosen; Partial +3 if all four options are correct but ONLY three chosen; Partial +2 if three or more options are correct but ONLY two chosen, both correct; Partial +1 if two or more correct but ONLY one chosen and it is correct; Zero 0 if unanswered; Negative -1 in all other cases. SECTION 3 (Max 16): FOUR questions, NUMERICAL VALUE, entered via mouse + on-screen virtual numeric keypad, 'If the numerical value has more than two decimal places, truncate/round-off the value to TWO decimal places'. Full +4 / Zero 0 in all other cases — NO negative marking. SECTION 4 (Max 16): FOUR Matching List Sets; List-I has FOUR entries (P)(Q)(R)(S), List-II has FIVE entries (1)-(5); four MCQ options, ONLY ONE satisfies. Full +4 / Zero 0 if unanswered / Negative -1 in all other cases. NOTE: Paper 1 2026 contained NO paragraph/comprehension section.
findings.implication: Four distinct scoring engines are required for Advanced Paper 1 alone: SINGLE_CORRECT(+3/-1), MULTI_CORRECT(partial ladder), NUMERICAL_2DP(no negative), MATCHING_LIST(+4/-1). Matching List needs a dedicated authoring UI: 4 left entries, 5 right entries, and 4 candidate permutation options — it is NOT a generic MCQ and needs its own render component.

findings.title: JEE Advanced 2026 Paper 2 is structurally different from Paper 1 — asymmetric papers
findings.detail: jeeadv.ac.in/documents/p2_english.pdf, per subject (60 marks, 18 questions; 54 questions / 180 marks total): SECTION 1 (Max 12) FOUR single-correct, +3/0/-1. SECTION 2 (Max 20) FIVE multi-correct, +4 with the identical +3/+2/+1 partial ladder, 0, -1. SECTION 3 (Max 20) FIVE numerical value, two-decimal truncate/round, +4 / 0, no negative. SECTION 4 (Max 8) TWO (02) question stems, TWO (02) questions per stem (= 4 sub-questions), each a NUMERICAL VALUE, Full +2 / Zero 0 in all other cases. So Paper 1 = 48 Q and Paper 2 = 54 Q, both 180 marks, both 3 hours (P1 09:00-12:00, P2 14:30-17:30 on 17 May 2026), both compulsory.
findings.implication: Data model needs a 'question stem / shared passage' entity: one stem with N child questions, each independently scored. Mark totals must be derived by summing per-section max marks, never assumed to be questions x 4. Paper 1 and Paper 2 templates must be separate blueprint records.

findings.title: JEE Advanced multi-correct negative marking changed from -2 to -1 between 2025 and 2026 — the pattern is explicitly not fixed
findings.detail: The 2026 Paper 1/2 Section 2 instructions read 'Negative Marks : -1 In all other cases'. JEE Advanced 2025 (IIT Kanpur) used -2 for multi-correct, and 2025 Paper 1 Section 2 had only 3 questions worth 12 marks vs 4 questions worth 16 in 2026. jeeadv.ac.in states only that 'The examination pattern for JEE (Advanced) 2026 will remain consistent with that of previous JEE (Advanced) examinations' — no numeric commitment; the exact counts and marking are disclosed only on-screen on exam day. Historically JEE Advanced has also used integer-answer (0-9), single-digit, paragraph/comprehension, and List-I/List-II matrix-match variants in different years.
findings.implication: Hardcoding Advanced marking is a guaranteed correctness bug within one year. Store marking as a versioned JSON rule object on the SECTION row (exam_year + paper + section -> rule), so a 2027 pattern shift is a data migration, not an app release. Also seed historical PYQ papers with their own year's rules so replayed PYQ mocks score authentically.

findings.title: Exact partial-marking algorithm for multi-correct (the version most competitors get wrong)
findings.detail: The rule is NOT 'marks proportional to correct options selected'. Let C = set of correct options, S = set of selected options. If S is empty -> 0. If S is not a subset of C (any wrong option selected) -> -1 (2026) / -2 (2025 and earlier), regardless of how many correct options were also selected. If S == C -> +4. Else (S is a proper non-empty subset of C): +3 only when |C| == 4 and |S| == 3; +2 when |C| >= 3 and |S| == 2; +1 when |C| >= 2 and |S| == 1. Worked example given verbatim in the paper: if (A),(B),(D) are the only correct answers, choosing A+B+D = +4; A+B = +2; A+D = +2; B+D = +2; A alone = +1; B alone = +1; D alone = +1; nothing = 0; any other combination = -1. Note the asymmetry: with |C| = 3, choosing 2 of 3 gives +2 (not +3), and there is no +3 tier at all unless all four options are correct. The widely circulated formula 'partial = 4 x selected_correct / total_correct' is WRONG (it would give 2.67 for 2-of-3).
findings.implication: Implement as a pure, unit-tested function scoreMultiCorrect(correctSet, selectedSet, rule) with the |C|/|S| lookup table, plus a golden-test suite built from the verbatim worked example in the 2026 paper. This is a headline differentiator: most competitor apps use the proportional formula and mis-score 2-of-3 cases.

findings.title: NEET UG 2026: no Section A/B, 180 compulsory questions, 180 minutes, pen-and-paper OMR
findings.detail: Information Bulletin NEET (UG)-2026, Chapter on Pattern of the Test, verbatim: 'The question paper will consist of 180 compulsory questions which must be attempted by the candidates in 180 minutes. (As per Letter CDN-20011/289/2024-Cordination-NMC dated 05.12.2025)'. Table: Physics 45 Q / 180 marks, Chemistry 45 Q / 180 marks, Biology (Botany & Zoology) 90 Q / 360 marks; Total 180 Q / 720 marks. Duration 02:00 PM to 05:00 PM. Type: 'MCQ with four options and single correct answer/best option'. Marking: +4 correct/most appropriate, -1 any incorrect option, 0 unanswered. Mode: 'single day/ single shift exam in PEN and PAPER mode as was conducted in 2025'. 13 mediums (English, Hindi, Assamese, Bengali, Gujarati, Kannada, Malayalam, Marathi, Odia, Punjabi, Tamil, Telugu, Urdu). PwD/PwBD get +1 hour. The 200-minute / Section-A-35Q + Section-B-15Q-choose-10 pattern used 2021-2024 is dead — do not implement it for current mocks.
findings.implication: NEET mock engine is much simpler than JEE: single section per subject, no NVQ, no partial marking. But Biology must be split into Botany (45) and Zoology (45) sub-buckets for analytics even though the paper presents 90 Biology questions — that split is how students and coaching institutes reason about it and matches our Subject>Chapter>Topic hierarchy.

findings.title: NEET's 'defective question' rules differ materially from JEE Main's and affect post-hoc rescoring
findings.detail: NEET UG 2026 bulletin verbatim: (i) if more than one option is found correct, +4 is awarded 'to only those who have marked any of the correct options'; (ii) if all options are found correct, +4 to all who ATTEMPTED the question; (iii) if none of the options is correct, or the question is wrong, or the question is dropped, +4 is given to ALL candidates who APPEARED 'irrespective of the fact whether the question has been attempted or not attempted'. JEE Main 2026 bulletin: dropped/incorrect question -> +4 to all candidates who appeared for that particular shift; if all options correct -> +4 to all who attempted.
findings.implication: Our scoring must support a post-publication 'answer key revision' event that recomputes historical attempts: per-question flags MULTI_KEY, ALL_CORRECT, DROPPED, each with its own award rule and a different eligible-population (attempted vs appeared). Build this as an idempotent Supabase Edge Function / SQL job with an audit trail, since it retroactively changes leaderboards and rewards.

findings.title: NTA CBT console spec (Appendix-VIII, JEE Main 2026 IB) — the exact behaviours to clone
findings.detail: Verbatim/near-verbatim: total duration 180 min (Paper 1) / 210 min (Paper 2A, 2B). 'The clock will be set at the server. The countdown timer in the top right corner of screen will display the remaining time available... When the timer reaches zero, the examination will end by itself. You will not be required to end or submit your examination.' Question Palette on the RIGHT shows per-question status; collapsible with '>' and reopened with '<'. Navigation: (a) clicking a question number in the palette goes there directly and 'does NOT save your answer to the current question'; (b) Save & Next saves then advances; (c) Mark for Review & Next saves, marks for review, then advances. Deselect an MCQ option by clicking it again or clicking Clear Response. To change an already-saved answer: select the question from the palette, click Clear Response, then re-answer. Sections are displayed on the TOP BAR; clicking a section name views it; the current section is highlighted; 'After clicking the Save and Next button on the last question for a Section, you will automatically be taken to the first question of the next section'; 'You can shuffle between sections and questions anytime during the examination'. A per-section summary legend appears above the palette. 'Question Paper' icon at top right shows the full paper. Profile image at top right switches the paper's language mid-exam; English is authoritative for evaluation. The physical keyboard is DISABLED for the entire duration — all input via mouse and on-screen virtual keyboard. Accessibility: dark/light mode toggle, font size increase/decrease, cursor trail toggle, cursor size, and a draggable Screen Magnifier. Blank rough sheets with a name/roll header are provided and must be surrendered. On computer/mouse malfunction, lost time is adjusted at the server.
findings.implication: This is our UI spec, verbatim. Key server-authoritative requirements: (1) timer anchored to server clock with drift correction and auto-submit at 0; (2) palette-click must NOT persist the in-progress answer — that single behaviour is what makes mocks feel real and is the most commonly missed detail; (3) auto-advance to next section on Save&Next at a section's last question; (4) free section switching (JEE Main/Advanced have no section locking, unlike CAT/GATE); (5) time-loss compensation implies our server must support extending a single attempt's deadline (useful for app crash / network loss on mobile).

findings.title: Question palette has exactly five states, with a non-obvious evaluation rule for 'Marked for Review'
findings.detail: Bulletin points 20-21: five statuses. Standard NTA legend (rendered as images in the PDF, so labels here are from the surrounding text plus the widely reproduced NTA legend): (1) You have not visited the question yet — grey/white; (2) You have not answered the question — red; (3) You have answered the question — green; (4) You have NOT answered the question but have marked it for review — purple/violet; (5) You have answered the question but marked it for review — purple with a green tick. Verbatim rule: 'A candidate has the option of answering a question and simultaneously Marked for Review, these answers WILL be considered for evaluation. However, if a candidate has simply put Marked for Review for a question without answering it, the corresponding question marked for review without an answer will NOT be considered for evaluation.' Also: 'The Marked for Review status for a question simply indicates that you would like to look at that question again.' Exact hex colours are not published by NTA (unverified) — the semantics, not the exact hex, are the fidelity requirement.
findings.implication: Model attempt state as a tuple (visited: bool, answer: nullable, marked_for_review: bool) and derive the 5 palette states, rather than storing a single enum — this makes state 5 (answered + marked) fall out correctly and guarantees answered+marked responses are scored. Given our 'no emoji / professional' design bar, pick a deliberate accessible palette (state must also be distinguishable by shape/number badge, not colour alone) but keep the same five semantics and the same legend wording.

findings.title: Calculators are BANNED in JEE Main 2026 — the on-screen calculator line in the bulletin was an NTA typo
findings.detail: NTA Public Notice dated 02 November 2025, verbatim: 'In the Appendix-VIII of the Information Bulletin for JEE (Main) - 2026 on Computer Based Test (CBT)... it has been mentioned that an onscreen standard calculator will be available during the Computer-Based Test (CBT). However, this feature forms part of the generic test conducting platform and does NOT apply to JEE (Main) conducted by the NTA, as the use of calculators in any form is not permitted in this examination. The revised Information Bulletin for JEE (Main) 2026 has been uploaded... NTA regrets the typographic error.' JEE Advanced likewise prohibits calculators; candidates get a scribble pad and only an on-screen virtual NUMERIC KEYPAD for entering numerical answers. NEET is OMR with no electronic aids (electronic watches with calculator facility are explicitly barred).
findings.implication: Do NOT ship an in-test calculator for JEE Main, JEE Advanced or NEET mocks. Ship instead: (a) an on-screen virtual numeric keypad component for NVQ entry (mouse/tap only, matching NTA), and (b) an optional digital scratchpad. Note the bulletin PDF still hosted at the October 2025 CDN path contains the erroneous calculator text — always cross-check bulletins against the Public Notices feed.

findings.title: JEE Main normalisation: percentile of the TOTAL raw score, per shift, to 7 decimal places
findings.detail: Appendix-VII, JEE (Main) 2026 IB. Percentile Score = 100 x (number of candidates who appeared in that Shift with raw score EQUAL TO OR LESS than the candidate) / (total number of candidates who appeared in that Shift). Topper of every shift gets exactly 100. 'The Percentile Scores will be calculated up to 7 decimal places to avoid the bunching effect and reduce ties.' Explicit warning: 'The Percentile of the Total shall NOT be an aggregate or average of the Percentile of the individual subject. The percentile score is not the same as the percentage of marks obtained.' Step-3: percentile scores of the Total Raw Score across all shifts are merged and called the NTA score. Subject-wise percentiles (Maths, Physics, Chemistry) are also published and are used only for tie-breaking. Raw scores can be negative (bulletin worked example shows lowest raw scores of -39, -38, -49, -44 and a candidate at 1.1034216 percentile with raw score -15). Merit uses the BEST of the two sessions' Total NTA Scores (not per-subject best). If cut-off percentiles differ across shifts, the LOWEST is applied to all shifts.
findings.implication: Our leaderboard/analytics must compute percentile within the cohort that took the SAME mock (our analogue of a shift), on the total, to 7 dp, and must gracefully display negative raw scores. Never average subject percentiles. For a multi-'shift' mock released in waves, replicate the merge step. Redis sorted sets are a natural fit but need 7-dp precision — store score as an integer of (percentile x 10^7) to avoid float ties.

findings.title: Three different tie-break chains — JEE Main, JEE Advanced, NEET — all must be implemented separately
findings.detail: JEE Main 2026 (IB section 2.4, Paper 1): 1) NTA score in Mathematics, 2) NTA score in Physics, 3) NTA score in Chemistry, 4) candidate with LESS proportion of attempted-incorrect to correct answers across all subjects, 5) same ratio in Mathematics, 6) in Physics, 7) in Chemistry, 8) otherwise SAME RANK is assigned. NEET UG 2026 (IB Chapter 8 s.2, per UGMEB/NMC Public Notice 13.06.2023 + NMC email 28.01.2026): a) higher marks/percentile in Biology (Botany & Zoology), b) Chemistry, c) Physics, d) less proportion of incorrect:correct across all subjects, e) same in Biology, f) Chemistry, g) Physics, h) if still tied, resolved by a RANDOM process guided by an independent expert committee. Age is NO LONGER a NEET tie-breaker (removed 2023). JEE Advanced 2026 (jeeadv.ac.in FAQ Q57): 1) higher POSITIVE marks (marks from correct answers before negatives are subtracted), 2) higher Mathematics score, 3) higher Physics score, 4) otherwise same rank.
findings.implication: Tie-break is a per-exam strategy object, not shared code. Note JEE Main leads with Maths, NEET leads with Biology, and JEE Advanced leads with total positive marks (which requires us to persist positive-marks-earned separately from net score on every attempt row — a column most implementations forget and cannot backfill).

findings.title: Post-submit flow: response sheet, provisional key, paid challenge window, final key, result
findings.detail: JEE Main 2026 (IB s.5.6): NTA displays recorded responses + attempted question paper on jeemain.nta.nic.in BEFORE the result, typically for 2-3 days; provisional answer key displayed alongside recorded responses, also 2-3 days; challenges cost a NON-REFUNDABLE Rs 200 per question, paid online, only via the official key-challenge link, and must carry justification/evidence; subject experts review; a FINAL answer key is declared and the result is compiled on it; no grievance entertained after result. NEET UG 2026 (IB Ch.15): scanned OMR answer sheets + recorded responses displayed for challenge at Rs 200 per question (OMR grading challenge) and Rs 200 per answer (answer key challenge), both non-refundable; if a challenge is upheld the key is revised for ALL candidates. JEE Advanced 2026 actual timeline: response sheet 21 May 2026, provisional answer key 25 May 2026 10:00, challenge window closed 26 May 2026 17:00, final answer key + result 01 June 2026 (challenge fee reported as Rs 500/question by some outlets and Rs 200 by others — unverified).
findings.implication: Ship a post-submit 'Response Sheet' screen mirroring NTA: question-by-question recorded response vs key, marks awarded, and a time-boxed 'Challenge this answer' flow routed to ADMIN. Because a sustained challenge revises the key for everyone, the rescore job must be idempotent, versioned, and must re-emit leaderboard/rewards deltas.

findings.title: 2026 calendar and scale reality: NEET 2026 was cancelled and re-run; NEET goes CBT in 2027
findings.detail: JEE Main 2026 Session 1: 21-29 January 2026, 13,55,293 registered, 13,04,653 appeared, results 16 Feb 2026, 12 candidates at 100 percentile (Paper 1). Session 2: 02-09 April 2026, results 20 April 2026, 26 candidates at 100 NTA score. JEE Advanced eligibility cut at top 2,50,000 across categories; General cutoff reported as 93.4123549 percentile (2026). JEE Advanced 2026 (IIT Roorkee) held 17 May 2026; 1,79,694 appeared in both papers; 56,880 qualified; qualifying CRL 92/360 (25.56%) aggregate with a per-subject minimum, OBC-NCL/EWS 82 (22.78%), SC/ST/PwD 46 (12.78%). NEET UG 2026 held 3 May 2026 was CANCELLED amid an alleged leak (Rajasthan SOG reportedly recovered a guess paper matching 140 questions); re-exam conducted 21 June 2026, key-challenge window closed 28 June 2026 23:50. Union Education Minister announced on 15 May 2026 that NEET-UG moves to CBT mode from 2027, affirmed by NTA to the Supreme Court; the 2027 Information Bulletin is still awaited.
findings.implication: Two product consequences: (1) our NEET mock UI should be built CBT-first now, because from 2027 the NTA console applies to NEET too — the same console component then serves all three exams and NEET students become the largest CBT-fidelity audience; (2) build an admin-facing 'exam calendar / pattern change' content model, because cancellations and re-exams are recurring events that invalidate scheduled test series mid-flight.

findings.title: Competitor partial-marking practice is inconsistent and frequently wrong
findings.detail: Widely republished secondary sources (infinitylearn, collegedunia, matrixedu, pw.live, aakash.ac.in as of July 2026) still state the JEE Advanced multi-correct penalty as -2, which is the 2025 rule and is WRONG for 2026 (-1). Several also publish the formula 'Partial marks = (4 x number of correct options selected) / (total number of correct options)', which contradicts the official ladder (it yields 2.67 for 2-of-3 where NTA awards +2, and 3.0 for 3-of-4 where NTA awards +3 only if all four options are correct). Allen and PhysicsWallah market 'NTA pattern' / 'replica' test series with performance analytics but publish no scoring spec; PW ran a free 'NEET Replica Test 2026'. Official practice consoles that DO reproduce the real interface: JEE Advanced 2026 practice tests on the TCS iON/digialm platform at https://cdn3.digialm.com//OnlineAssessment/index.html?32044@@M217 (Paper 1) and ...?32044@@M219 (Paper 2), linked from jeeadv.ac.in Resources; NTA hosts mock tests at nta.ac.in (Quiz/Abhyas) and physical Test Practice Centres.
findings.implication: Scoring correctness on multi-correct is a credible, demonstrable differentiator. Publish our marking rules in-app per test (as NTA does on-screen) and show a per-question marks-awarded breakdown in the solution view so students can verify. Use the two official digialm practice consoles as the visual/behavioural reference for our test player.

findings.title: All-India Rank predictor: the input set and the honest accuracy ceiling
findings.detail: To predict a JEE Main AIR you need, at minimum: (1) raw marks out of 300 (or per-subject raw marks), (2) the exact session/date/shift the student attempted (shift difficulty differs and normalisation is per shift), (3) the candidate's category (GEN/OBC-NCL/EWS/SC/ST/PwD) and gender and home state for category rank and state-quota outcomes, (4) total appeared count for that year (13,04,653 appeared in Session 1 2026; ~15.5 lakh commonly used as the denominator across both sessions), (5) historical marks-vs-percentile and percentile-vs-AIR anchor tables from prior years, (6) our own cohort's marks distribution for the same mock as a proxy shift. The naive conversion published everywhere is Rank ~= ((100 - percentile) / 100) x TotalCandidates + 1, e.g. 95 percentile x 12,00,000 -> ~60,000. It is only valid if our cohort distribution matches the national one, which it will not (self-selected, coaching-skewed). For a college predictor you additionally need JoSAA/CSAB opening-closing ranks by institute-branch-category-quota-gender-round (6 rounds + CSAB special rounds) and for NEET the MCC 15% AIQ plus state-quota counselling data. NEET rank prediction is simpler: no normalisation (single shift, OMR), so marks-to-rank is a near-deterministic mapping from the published rank list, and the main input is just marks + category + the year's appeared count.
findings.implication: Ship an anchored predictor, not a naive percentile x N: calibrate our cohort's marks distribution against published national marks-vs-percentile anchor points (e.g. the year's 99.5/99/95 percentile marks) via monotone interpolation, and always surface a confidence interval plus 'based on N students in this mock'. Collect category/gender/home-state/target-exam at onboarding — retrofitting these later on 10k+ users is painful and they are also valuable for RBAC-scoped analytics.

recommendations: Model marking as data, never code. Schema: exam_pattern(id, exam, year, paper) -> pattern_section(id, pattern_id, ordinal, name, max_marks, question_count, question_type) -> marking_rule(section_id, jsonb). Rule JSON carries {full, zero_on_unanswered, negative, partial_ladder[], numerical_precision, negative_on_numerical}. Seed four rows for JEE Advanced 2026 P1, four for P2, one per JEE Main subject-section, one for NEET. A 2027 pattern change becomes an INSERT, not a release. Store the pattern_id on every mock test so PYQ replays score by their own year's rules.

Implement scoreMultiCorrect() exactly per the official ladder — |C|=4 and |S|=3 -> +3; |C|>=3 and |S|=2 -> +2; |C|>=2 and |S|=1 -> +1; S==C -> +4; any element of S outside C -> negative; S empty -> 0 — and lock it with a golden test suite generated from the verbatim worked example in the JEE Advanced 2026 paper (correct = {A,B,D}: AB=+2, AD=+2, BD=+2, A=+1, B=+1, D=+1, ABD=+4, {}=0, anything else=-1). Explicitly reject the proportional formula. Run the same function server-side in a Postgres function or Edge Function so the client can never be the source of truth for marks.

Build one NTA-faithful test player component reused across JEE Main / JEE Advanced / NEET-2027-CBT, implementing exactly: server-anchored countdown (top-right, minutes) with auto-submit at zero and no manual end required; five-state question palette on the right with collapse/expand; Save & Next; Mark for Review & Next; Clear Response; palette-number navigation that explicitly does NOT persist the current in-progress answer; section tabs on the top bar with free switching and auto-advance to the next section's first question after Save & Next on a section's last question; per-section summary above the palette; a 'Question Paper' full-view; a pre-test Instructions screen; and a final submit confirmation summarising answered / not answered / marked counts per section.

Ship NO calculator. Instead ship (a) an on-screen virtual numeric keypad for numerical-value entry that is mouse/tap-only, matching NTA, and (b) an optional digital rough-work scratchpad. Enforce input rules per exam: JEE Main NVQ = integer, evaluated after round-to-nearest-integer; JEE Advanced numerical = truncate/round to TWO decimal places with exact match at 2 dp. Keep font-size control, a dark/light toggle and a magnifier, mirroring NTA's documented accessibility set — these double as genuine mobile accessibility wins.

Persist an attempt state tuple per question — (visited, answer, marked_for_review, time_spent_ms, answer_change_count, first_seen_at, last_saved_at) — and derive the five palette states rather than storing an enum. Also persist positive_marks_earned separately from net_marks on the attempt row: JEE Advanced tie-breaking needs positive marks first, and it cannot be backfilled once responses are archived. Store the raw response set for multi-correct (array of option ids), not a boolean correct flag, so a key revision can rescore losslessly.

Implement three separate tie-break strategy objects keyed by exam: JEE Main (Maths -> Physics -> Chemistry -> incorrect:correct ratio overall -> Maths -> Physics -> Chemistry -> equal rank), JEE Advanced (positive marks -> Maths -> Physics -> equal rank), NEET (Biology -> Chemistry -> Physics -> incorrect:correct ratio overall -> Biology -> Chemistry -> Physics -> deterministic pseudo-random seeded by attempt id). Explicitly do NOT use age for NEET — that criterion was removed in 2023.

Compute mock-test percentile the NTA way: percentile of TOTAL raw score within the cohort that took the same mock, to 7 decimal places, never an average of subject percentiles; publish subject-wise percentiles alongside for tie-breaks only; support and correctly render NEGATIVE raw totals. For Redis leaderboards store score as an integer (percentile x 10^7) to avoid float collisions at 10k+ concurrent students.

Build an idempotent, versioned answer-key-revision pipeline before launch, not after. It must support per-question flags MULTI_KEY (+4 to anyone who marked any correct option), ALL_CORRECT (+4 to all who attempted) and DROPPED (+4 to all who appeared — for JEE Main scoped to the shift), rescore all affected attempts transactionally, write an audit row, and re-emit leaderboard and rewards-coin deltas. Pair it with a student-facing post-submit Response Sheet (recorded response vs key, marks awarded per question) and a time-boxed ADMIN-routed 'challenge this answer' flow mirroring NTA's Rs 200/question window.

Author the JEE Main blueprint as exactly 3 subjects x (Section A 20 MCQ + Section B 5 NVQ), all 25 compulsory, 300 marks, 180 min; JEE Advanced 2026 P1 as 3 x (4 single-correct / 4 multi-correct / 4 numerical-2dp / 4 matching-list) = 48 Q / 180 marks and P2 as 3 x (4 / 5 / 5 / 2 stems x 2) = 54 Q / 180 marks, 180 min each; NEET as Physics 45 + Chemistry 45 + Botany 45 + Zoology 45 = 180 Q / 720 marks / 180 min with no sections. Validate blueprints at save time (sum of section max_marks must equal declared total) so ADMIN cannot ship a malformed paper.

Add first-class content types for Matching List (List-I with 4 entries P/Q/R/S, List-II with 5 entries 1-5, plus 4 permutation options) and for Question Stem / shared paragraph with N independently-scored child questions. Both are required for JEE Advanced fidelity and neither is expressible as a generic MCQ. Given heavy LaTeX, render both lists and stems through the same math pipeline and cache rendered output.

Collect exam target (JEE Main / JEE Advanced / NEET), category (GEN/OBC-NCL/EWS/SC/ST/PwD), gender, home state and target year at onboarding. These are the required inputs for any credible rank/college predictor and for category-scoped percentile analytics, and retrofitting them across 10,000+ existing users is materially harder than asking once.

Build the NEET experience CBT-first now. NEET-UG is announced to move to computer-based testing from 2027, which means our single NTA console component will serve the largest cohort in the market from next cycle, while 2026-pattern OMR practice remains a thin presentational variant of the same engine.
pitfalls: Hardcoding JEE Advanced marking constants. The multi-correct penalty was -2 in 2025 and -1 in 2026; Paper 1 Section 2 had 3 questions in 2025 and 4 in 2026; Paper 1 carried no paragraph section in 2026 while Paper 2 used question stems. jeeadv.ac.in commits only to being 'consistent with previous examinations' and discloses exact counts and marking on-screen on exam day. Any constant in code will be wrong within twelve months.

Using the proportional partial-marking formula (4 x selected_correct / total_correct). It is the most-republished formula on the web and it is wrong: with 3 correct options and 2 selected, NTA awards +2, not 2.67; and +3 is only ever awarded when ALL FOUR options are correct and exactly three are chosen. Selecting even one wrong option voids all partial credit and applies the full negative.

Implementing the retired NEET Section A / Section B (35 + 15-choose-10, 200 minutes) pattern. That structure was scrapped after 2024; NEET 2025 and 2026 are 180 compulsory questions in 180 minutes with no optional choice. Equally, implementing JEE Main Section B as 10 questions with any-5 optional — the choice was removed in 2025 and Section B now carries -1 negative marking, which it never did in the optional era.

Shipping an in-test calculator. NTA Public Notice dated 02 November 2025 states the on-screen calculator described in Appendix-VIII of the JEE Main 2026 Information Bulletin 'forms part of the generic test conducting platform and does NOT apply to JEE (Main)' and that 'the use of calculators in any form is not permitted'. The stale bulletin PDF still on the CDN contains the erroneous text — trusting the bulletin alone reproduces NTA's own bug.

Making palette-click save the current answer. In the real console, clicking a question number in the palette navigates WITHOUT saving; only Save & Next and Mark for Review & Next persist. Students lose answers to this in the real exam and expect the same behaviour in a faithful mock. Getting it 'helpfully' wrong is the single most common fidelity failure.

Dropping 'answered and marked for review' responses at scoring time. NTA explicitly evaluates them; only marked-for-review-WITHOUT-an-answer is excluded. Collapsing the five palette states into a single enum is what causes this bug.

Averaging subject percentiles to produce a total percentile. The JEE Main bulletin states outright that the Percentile of the Total 'shall NOT be an aggregate or average of the Percentile of the individual subject'. Percentile must be computed on the total raw score within the shift/cohort, to 7 decimal places, and raw totals can legitimately be negative.

Client-authoritative timing or scoring. NTA's clock is server-set and the exam auto-ends at zero with no user action; time lost to a malfunction is compensated at the server. On mobile with backgrounding, network loss and clock skew, any client-side timer will be gamed and any client-side scoring will be tampered with. Deadlines and marks must live in Postgres/Edge Functions with RLS, with an explicit admin-visible mechanism to extend a single attempt.

Treating tie-breaking as shared logic. Three exams, three different chains, with different lead subjects (Maths / positive-marks / Biology) and different terminal behaviour (JEE Main and JEE Advanced assign the SAME rank; NEET resolves by a random process under an expert committee). Also do not use age as a NEET tie-breaker — that was removed by the UGMEB/NMC public notice of 13 June 2023.

Assuming the answer key is immutable. Both NTA exams run paid public challenge windows (Rs 200 per question) after which keys are revised for all candidates, and questions can be declared multi-key, all-correct or dropped — each with a different award rule and a different eligible population (attempted vs appeared, and for JEE Main scoped to a single shift). Without an idempotent rescore pipeline and audit trail, a key revision corrupts leaderboards and already-issued reward coins.

Predicting All India Rank with the naive Rank = (100 - percentile)/100 x TotalCandidates formula on our own cohort. Our user base is self-selected and coaching-skewed, so its raw distribution is not the national distribution; without anchoring to published national marks-vs-percentile points the predictions will be confidently wrong and will destroy trust.

Assuming the 2026 exam calendar is stable. NEET UG 2026 held on 3 May 2026 was cancelled amid an alleged paper leak and re-run on 21 June 2026, and NEET moves to CBT from 2027. Test-series scheduling, streaks and contests keyed to fixed official dates need an admin-editable exam-calendar entity that can absorb cancellations and re-exams mid-cycle.
openQuestions: Exact hex values of the five NTA question-palette states are not published in any official document — the legend appears only as a raster image in the bulletin. We should sample them from the official digialm practice consoles (jeeadv Paper 1 M217 / Paper 2 M219) or from NTA's mock test at nta.ac.in, then choose an accessible equivalent that keeps the same semantics and legend wording. Colour alone must not encode state (WCAG).

The exact wording and layout of NTA's final submit confirmation dialog (per-section answered / not answered / marked-for-review counts, and whether a second confirmation is required) is not documented in the bulletin text and needs to be captured from a live official mock run.

JEE Advanced 2026 answer-key challenge fee is reported inconsistently in secondary media (Rs 500 vs Rs 200 per question). The authoritative figure is in the JEE (Advanced) 2026 Information Brochure, which we did not parse.

JEE Advanced 2026 per-subject minimum qualifying marks: the aggregate figures (CRL 92/360 = 25.56%, OBC-NCL/EWS 82 = 22.78%, SC/ST/PwD 46 = 12.78%) and appeared/qualified counts (1,79,694 / 56,880) come from secondary sources; one source quotes the per-subject minimum as 8 marks but calls it 7.30% when 8/120 is 6.67%. Needs confirmation from the official jeeadv result notification.

The NEET UG 2026 re-exam on 21 June 2026 was reported as running 14:00-17:15 (195 minutes) rather than the bulletin's 14:00-17:00 (180 minutes). Unverified — needs the NTA re-exam public notice to confirm whether extra time was granted and why.

The NEET UG 2027 CBT Information Bulletin is not yet published. Unknown: whether it will be single-shift or multi-shift (multi-shift would introduce NEET normalisation for the first time, changing our percentile engine), whether sections are introduced, and whether the console will match the JEE Main console exactly.

Whether NTA's CBT console enforces any section-entry locking or per-section time limits for JEE Main/Advanced. The bulletin says candidates 'can shuffle between sections and questions anytime', which implies none — but this should be confirmed against a live mock before we build section navigation.

How competitors actually implement multi-correct scoring internally (Allen, PhysicsWallah, Aakash, Marks, Embibe) is not publicly documented; only their marketing pages and their published exam-pattern articles are visible, and several of those articles state the stale -2 rule. A hands-on comparison of a paid test series would be needed to confirm whether the product-level scoring is also wrong.

Whether NTA publishes per-shift appeared counts and marks distributions in a machine-readable form. If not, our rank predictor must depend on scraped or manually curated marks-vs-percentile anchor tables, which is a maintenance and reliability liability worth costing before committing to the feature.
